source: NCERT Class X, Science, Ch. 13 (Our Environment).

sections.heading: 1. Ecosystem — Components
points: An **ecosystem** = all living organisms (biotic) + their physical surroundings (abiotic) interacting together (e.g. forest, pond); may be **natural** or **artificial** (crop field, aquarium).
**Biotic components:** **producers** (green plants, make food), **consumers** (herbivores, carnivores, omnivores, parasites), **decomposers** (bacteria, fungi — break down dead matter).
**Abiotic components:** temperature, light, water, air, soil, minerals.

sections.heading: 2. Food Chains, Food Webs and Energy Flow
points: **Food chain** — a series of organisms feeding on one another (producer → herbivore → carnivore); each level = a **trophic level**.
**Food web** — interconnected food chains.
**Energy flow is unidirectional**; the **10% law** (Lindeman) — only ~10% of energy passes to the next trophic level (rest lost as heat/life processes).
Food chains are usually short (3–4 steps) because energy diminishes at each level.
**Biological magnification** — harmful chemicals (pesticides) increase in concentration up the trophic levels (top consumers, including humans, most affected).

sections.heading: 3. Waste and Its Disposal
points: **Biodegradable** substances — broken down by decomposers/microbes (e.g. paper, food, cotton, cow dung).
**Non-biodegradable** substances — not decomposed by microbes (e.g. plastic, glass, DDT, metals) — persist and pollute; harm ecosystems.
Improper waste management causes pollution and health hazards; the need for recycling and safe disposal.

sections.heading: 4. Ozone Layer and Its Depletion
points: **Ozone (O₃)** in the upper atmosphere (stratosphere) shields Earth from harmful **ultraviolet (UV) radiation** (which causes skin cancer, cataracts).
Ozone is destroyed by **chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)** — used in refrigerators, ACs, aerosols.
The **Montreal Protocol (1987)** — international agreement to reduce CFC production/emission.
Ozone is both protective (stratosphere) and, at ground level, a pollutant.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Ecosystem = biotic + abiotic; producers, consumers, decomposers.
10% law: only ~10% energy passes to next trophic level; energy flow unidirectional.
Biological magnification = pesticides increase up the food chain (humans most affected).
Biodegradable (decomposed) vs non-biodegradable (plastic, DDT, glass).
Ozone blocks UV; CFCs destroy ozone; Montreal Protocol (1987).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Only about **10% of energy** passes to the next trophic level (10% law).
**Biological magnification** makes **top consumers/humans** most affected by pesticides.
**Decomposers** (bacteria/fungi) recycle nutrients; **producers** make food.
**CFCs deplete the ozone layer**; the **Montreal Protocol (1987)** controls them.
